sa-cricetulus-griseus.title: Chinese Dwarf Hamster
sa-cricetulus-griseus.summary: A small, slender dwarf hamster with a short tail. Chinese hamsters are not naturally sociable and are best kept on their own.
rows: Body about 2.8–4.6 in (72–116 mm) plus a short tail; 20–35 g

At least 100 × 50 cm floor (about 40 × 20 in) and 50 cm tall; bigger is better. A tank with a mesh lid works well (gaps under 1 cm). At least 20 cm (8 in) of dust-extracted paper, wood-pulp or hemp bedding for burrowing, plus hides and a sand bath. Avoid tube systems and fluffy bedding. Wheel: solid, 25–27 cm across

Hamster pellets or a seed mix made for hamsters, with small portions of fresh vegetables (about the size of the hamster's ear); scatter food to encourage foraging. Never grapes or rhubarb. Fresh water from a bottle at all times
Best kept alone; Chinese hamsters are not naturally sociable
Can bite if woken or handled roughly; let it wake fully first and handle gently. Adults should supervise children
Northern China; the wider Chinese striped hamster group ranges from southern Siberia through Mongolia to North Korea

sa-phodopus-sungorus.title: Winter White (Djungarian) Dwarf Hamster
sa-phodopus-sungorus.summary: A small dwarf hamster with a dark stripe down its back and furry feet; in the wild its coat turns white in winter (pets kept under house lights usually don't change). It's known as one of the most tamable hamsters.
rows: Body about 2.8–3.5 in (70–90 mm); about 19–45 g
About 1–3 years in captivity, sometimes longer

At least 100 × 50 cm floor (about 40 × 20 in) and 50 cm tall; bigger is better. A tank with a mesh lid works well (gaps under 1 cm). At least 20 cm (8 in) of dust-extracted paper, wood-pulp or hemp bedding for burrowing, plus hides and a sand bath. Avoid tube systems and fluffy bedding. Wheel: solid, 22–25 cm across. Dwarfs climb poorly, so keep levels low

Hamster pellets or a seed mix made for hamsters, with small portions of fresh vegetables (about the size of the hamster's ear); scatter food to encourage foraging. Never grapes or rhubarb. Fresh water from a bottle at all times
Same-sex pairs can sometimes live together, but co-housing can cause stress and fights; a single hamster with a large, enriched enclosure is safest
One of the more tamable hamsters; still handle gently and supervise children
Steppes and meadows of Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Siberia and Manchuria

sa-phodopus-roborovskii.title: Roborovski (Robo) Dwarf Hamster
sa-phodopus-roborovskii.summary: The smallest pet hamster, a speedy little desert dweller from Central Asia. Robos are fun to watch and especially need a large sand area.
rows: About 2.5 in (6.3 cm) and about 16 g

At least 100 × 50 cm floor (about 40 × 20 in) and 50 cm tall; bigger is better. A tank with a mesh lid works well (gaps under 1 cm). At least 20 cm (8 in) of dust-extracted paper, wood-pulp or hemp bedding for burrowing, plus hides and a sand bath. Avoid tube systems and fluffy bedding. A large sand area is especially important. Wheel: solid, 20–22 cm across

Hamster pellets or a seed mix made for hamsters, with small portions of fresh vegetables (about the size of the hamster's ear); scatter food to encourage foraging. Never grapes or rhubarb. Fresh water from a bottle at all times
Sometimes kept in same-sex sibling pairs, but they don't need company and can fall out; separate permanently if they fight
Can bite if woken or handled roughly; let it wake fully first and handle gently. Adults should supervise children
Deserts of Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Tuva, Mongolia and Xinjiang, China)

sa-phodopus-dwarf.title: Dwarf Hamster (Phodopus)
sa-phodopus-dwarf.summary: Dwarf hamsters are small, round, short-tailed hamsters with furry feet from the dry steppes and semi-deserts of central Asia. Fancy and color varieties (cinnamon, pinto, platinum, blackberry and others) are bred from the pet dwarf species, and all need the same basic care: a roomy enclosure with deep bedding to burrow in.
rows: At least 100 × 50 cm floor (about 40 × 20 in) and 50 cm tall; bigger is better. A tank with a mesh lid works well (gaps under 1 cm). At least 20 cm (8 in) of dust-extracted paper, wood-pulp or hemp bedding for burrowing, plus hides and a sand bath. Avoid tube systems and fluffy bedding. Wheel: solid, about 20–25 cm across. Dwarfs climb poorly, so keep platforms low

Hamster pellets or a seed mix made for hamsters, with small portions of fresh vegetables (about the size of the hamster's ear); scatter food to encourage foraging. Never grapes or rhubarb. Fresh water from a bottle at all times

They can fall out and fight, and fights are serious; same-sex pairs only, with plenty of space, and separate them permanently if they fight. A single hamster in a large, enriched enclosure is the safe choice
Handle gently and low over a soft surface; let it wake fully first. Adults should supervise children
Mostly active at night; does not hibernate
Steppes, forests and semi-deserts of Mongolia, Siberia, China and Kazakhstan
notes: Dwarf hamsters have a scent gland on the belly that can look like a small waxy spot; this is normal.
A sand bath helps keep the coat clean.
